articles.title: Thieves on the Hunt for GPUs Stole Nvidia Trucks, but All They Got Was 20 Tons of Sand
articles.summary: It's no secret that GPUs are worth their weight in gold right now, with the ongoing RAM crisis shooting prices through the stratosphere. That's probably what some thieves were thinking too, as they stole two Nvidia-branded trailers thinking they were getting a load of expensive GPUs. But they just ended up with sand.
articles.body:
It's no secret that GPUs are worth their weight in gold right now, with the ongoing RAM crisis shooting prices through the stratosphere. That's probably what some thieves were thinking too, as they stole two Nvidia-branded trailers thinking they were getting a load of expensive GPUs. But they just ended up with sand.

According to Wired , the thieves stole two trailers branded with Nvidia and PlusAI's logos in Newark, California last week, but rather than expensive hardware, they were loaded up with 20,000 pounds of sand each. That's a weird thing for a tech company to be loading a trailer with, but Nvidia and PlusAI have been teaming up to test autonomous trucks, and the trailers full of sand were being used to simulate loads.

PlusAI was notified that the sand was missing when an executive got a text message from a friend, who had seen the trailers parked outside of their Newark-based office. PlusAI was then able to recover the trailers, and all the sand within, as it seems the thieves abandoned them. No arrests have been made.

The most expensive part of the setup – the tech-equipped trucks themselves – were parked inside the warehouse, and were left alone.

As AI hardware has continued to go up in price to fuel data center growth, these thefts have grown more popular, according to a report about Q2 2026 theft risk from Verisk CargoNet : "Organized groups also continued targeting enterprise-grade computer and networking equipment, components and cryptocurrency mining hardware. These shipments may be worth several million dollars but frequently move through the supply chain as conventional dry freight, creating a significant mismatch between their financial value and their ordinary transportation and security profile."

These thefts probably aren't helping with the cost of hardware. RAM prices have continued to climb since the start of 2026, and Nvidia graphics cards specifically have had massive price jumps this year. Plus, it doesn't seem likely that Nvidia will be releasing new graphics cards any time soon , either.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: The Simpsons Kicks Off an Unprecedented 38th Season With a new Episode Guest-Starring a Delightful Emma Thompson
articles.summary: The Simpsons kicks off Season 38 with a mostly standard premiere episode that's carried by the delightfully British guest star Emma Thompson.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for The Simpsons Season 38, Episode 1!

Nothing is certain in life but death, taxes, and new seasons of The Simpsons. It's pretty incredible to think that this iconic animated sitcom has crossed the 800-episode mark and is now entering its 38th season. That said, the series doesn't do anything particularly noteworthy to ring in the new season. "The Children's Book Job" settles for delivering a fairly standard late-era Simpsons adventure, one that's mostly carried on the back of its guest star.

The conflict this week comes as Marge (Julie Kavner) is no sooner sworn in as PTA president than the town learns Springfield Elementary is about to be shut down. That in itself seems like a decent premise for a new episode. How do you save this beloved Springfield institution? Should the town even want to, given how legendarily terrible Springfield Elementary is?

Every Time The Simpsons Predicted the Future

But that's not the direction writer Dan Vebber opts to go with this particular storyline. Instead, Marge and her fellow parents put all their eggs in the basket of beloved children's book author Constance Clavinger (Emma Thompson). Apparently, having Constance read her latest creation in public is the key to keeping Springfield Elementary's doors open? I wish I knew that when my local district was deciding to shut down my daughter's school...

It's a slightly weird and random pivot, but whatever. As mentioned before, it's really all about this week's celebrity guest voice. Thompson is a real hoot as Constance, an eccentric personality who's both charmingly British and enough of a drunken mess to give Homer (Dan Castellaneta) a run for his money. We also get a brief cameo from Colin Jost, but this is really Thompson's show to steal at the end of the day. She brings her A-game, making the most of her character's many wild mood swings and even belting out a tune with Castellaneta for good measure.

Plot-wise, "The Children's Book Job" is nothing special. This episode is yet another opportunity for Homer to prove he can be reliable and dependable and isn't fully checked out of the fatherhood game. I do appreciate that it doesn't take the cynical route, but instead focuses on Homer earnestly trying to manage Constance's nonstop brand of mischief. The ending is also sweet, as Homer manages to pierce through Constance's jaded heart and convince her not to sabotage her life's work. But still, this is nothing we haven't seen 1000 times before on the Homer/Marge front.

There are a few other noteworthy moments worth calling out in the premiere. It makes solid use of the wider Springfield supporting cast, whether it's Moe (Hank Azaria) calling for a Squid Game-style bloodbath or Snake (Azaria) briefly allying himself with Homer's cause. It would be pretty funny if the series actually followed up on that plot thread and the destruction of Homer's beloved car, but somehow, I doubt that'll happen. I also got a kick out of Marge's passive-agressive responses to Lisa's (Yeardley Smith) various helpful suggestions.

But if there's anything in this episode that stands out as much as Thompson's character, it's the brief chase sequence where Homer hallucinates a journey through various children's books. It's a well-animated bit with fun nods to everything from classics like Madeleine and Richard Scarry to modern fare like Captain Underpants. That's one way to spice up an otherwise textbook Homer storyline.

articles.title: God of War Laufey Features Kratos in an Ancient Greek Setting, Sparking Speculation Over the Game's Story — and Praise for His Big Bushy Beard
articles.body:
Fans are discussing a new God of War Laufey screenshot featuring fan-favorite hero Kratos, in a setting resembling Ancient Greece.

The image was revealed today via the PlayStation blog , alongside details of the game's preorder bonuses and digital deluxe edition. The screenshot shows Laufey's eponymous heroine with Kratos, with the pair standing in what looks to be a Greek temple.

Why is this interesting? Well, because Laufey is supposed to be dead and separated from Kratos, and she never visited Ancient Greece during his time there, which occured long before they met. So, what's going on?

Firstly, while Laufey is very much the star of this new game, fans have already seen Kratos pop up a couple of times at its beginning, in footage released back when the game was revealed in June . First, the bearded demigod can be seen burning Laufey's body on a funeral pyre, an event which took place at the start of the 2018 God of War game.

Laufey then re-awakens in the Everywhen — a heavenly place that serves as an afterlife for gods of all mythologies — and it's here that Kratos visits her again in a moment of need, albeit only momentarily. When this scene was shown earlier this year, however, it was not clear if Kratos would feature further in the game, or this was something of a one-off.

Today's screenshot answers that question, but then asks several more. Which version of Kratos is this? Is it the version that's still alive and living through the events of 2018's God of War and its sequel Ragnarök? If so, when exactly in his timeline does this take place? Alternatively, could this be a version of Kratos that has also found himself in the Everywhen via other means (perhaps after his eventual final death)?

And what about that Ancient Greek setting? Is this a corner of the Everywhen that Laufey will visit, themed around Greek mythology? Will other familiar faces from the first God of War trilogy make a reappearance here too?

"Where the hell are they?" God of War fan Iluminado_Horn wrote on video game forum ResetEra. "In Greece? After Ragnarok?"

"Laufey dreams/hallucinates of Kratos, it was shown on the gameplay reveal," responded another fan, Patitoloco. "This could be anywhere in the game, or a flashback."

Last, but certainly not least, this image has sparked praise for Kratos' exquisitely bushy beard, which has been rendered on PlayStation 5 Pro in fine detail. While this isn't our first time gazing at the game running on PS5 Pro, it is certainly impressive when you take a moment to appreciate it.

God of War Laufey will launch exclusively for PlayStation 5 early next year, on February 16, 2027.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 Dev Acknowledges That Chaos Is Harder to Fight Than Tyranids, Confirms Plan to Do Something About It
articles.summary: Ever since Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2’s 2024 launch, players have said that the Chaos enemies are harder to fight than the Tyranids. Well, now Space Marine 2’s game director has come out and admitted that is indeed the case — and confirmed plans to do something about it.
articles.body:
Ever since Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2’s 2024 launch, players have said that the Chaos enemies are harder to fight than the Tyranids. Well, now Space Marine 2’s game director has come out and admitted that is indeed the case — and confirmed plans to do something about it.

For the uninitiated, the Tyranids are a swarm-type enemy type that packs the screen with a mix of smaller foes and much bigger, harder-hitting foes. There’s a bloody minded pleasure that comes from chewing through scores of Tyranid enemies as a Space Marine, sweeping your Power Sword through xenos flesh, parrying a strike that gives you a clean response, and — my personal favorite — punching those Tyranids in the face with my Power Fist.

In contrast, the Thousand Sons present a more measured challenge. You are, after all, going up against fellow Space Marines here and their daemonic forces; they’re supposed to be tough. When those Terminators spawn and spam their missile barrage, playing against Chaos can feel like pulling teeth. The Thousand Sons are less of a 'switch your brain off and cleave through it' proposition, and more of a, 'if Space Marine 2 wanted to be a bit like Elden Ring, it would probably go a little like this.'

Warhammer 40,000 11th Edition Cinematic Trailer: All Shots of the Emperor

The effect is more pronounced the harder the difficulty you play. At easier difficulties, the Tyranids and Chaos are much of a muchness in terms of challenge. But ramp the difficulty up — which you need to do for certain levels of progression in Space Marine 2 — and Chaos becomes an absolute bloody nightmare, whereas the Tyranids often still feel manageable.

For this reason, Space Marine 2 players have for years now said the Tyranids are more fun to play against than Chaos , and I certainly agree. But in a Reddit AMA , game director Dmitry Grigorenko not only acknowledged that Chaos are harder, but said there is work being done to tweak the balance between the two enemy factions.

“We understand that Chaos is more difficult to fight against Tyranids, yes,” Grigorenko said . “There will be some pass on this in the future. I don't think it will be about bots being good vs Chaos specifically, though.”

That latter part of the answer is a response to the suggestion that Space Marine 2 should balance Chaos Operations (PvE missions) so it’s easier to fight against them as a solo player. With that ruled out, what could Grigorenko be talking about here? Perhaps it’s about a nerf to the entire faction, whether it be toughness, damage, or even spawn intensity. There are lots of things Saber could do here, although the fundamentals of how Chaos works in the game versus the Tyranids won’t change. Chaos are Space Marines after all.

I suspect that no matter what Saber does here, the Tyranids will always be more fun to fight than Chaos. That’s because you simply can't beat the feeling that comes from carving your way through the swarm, or pumping scores of alien monsters with bolter fire. That’s kind of the way this works. Still, I wouldn’t mind a tweak that makes me wince a little less whenever I’m up against Chaos.

My thoughts have inevitably turned to Space Marine 3, which is in development. What will be the “swarm” enemy here? Most believe Space Marine 3 will feature the Necrons, based on hints sprinkled throughout Space Marine 2. But what other factions would fit the bill? A return to the Orks seen in Space Marine 1? (Orks are the primary antagonist of the 11th edition of the Warhammer 40,000 tabletop game.) How about a focus on the relentless Death Guard and swarms of shuffling Plaguebearers?

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: GTA 6 Has an 'Advanced' Weather System, but How Will It Work?
articles.summary: GTA 6 is confirmed to have an "advanced" weather system, leading many to wonder if we're going to get tropical storms.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is confirmed to have an "advanced" weather system, leading many to wonder if we're going to get tropical storms.

Game Informer has confirmed that GTA 6 will be the magazine's cover story this month and as a result, it will feature a treasure trove of new details about the game. The 14-page story will feature exclusive interviews and screenshots and while we're still waiting to find out all the specifics, Game Informer did confirm it will dive into the game's "advanced weather systems that simulate Florida’s less sunny weather phenomena."

Although we'll have to wait to learn more about what that means, this tidbit has resulted in a flurry of speculation. GTA 6 is set in Leonida, a fictional version of Florida, which has many wondering if there will be intense weather systems such as hurricanes. Game Informer's tease suggests that Rockstar is finally going to reveal the limits of its weather system, but one has to imagine it will go further than previous Rockstar titles.

GTA 6 is a technically ambitious game, but having something like a hurricane outside of a scripted event or mission seems like a daunting task for the developers. It could change the map, create unique gameplay obstacles, and really stir things up in complex ways. Up until now, Rockstar has been cagey when asked about its plans for weather. It's possible the studio was still trying to finetune these systems before saying anything, as to avoid getting anyone's hopes up, but hopefully it has designed something that goes beyond a simple rain shower.

Red Dead Redemption 2 had some pretty intense storms which featured intimidating lightning and thunder, big gusts of wind, and spooky dark clouds. The game also featured snow and dust storms in relevant parts of the map. It's unlikely we'll see either of those return in a parody of the sunshine state, but it's clear that Rockstar likes to create dynamic circumstances to make the world feel more alive and potentially add more challenges.

Game Informer's story goes live tomorrow, September 29, so we'll be able to mull over all of the details soon. However, there are no shortage of details about GTA 6's in IGN's own preview of the game from earlier this summer. It's unclear if or when we'll get another trailer for the game, but hopefully, it won't be too much longer.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: The Witcher 3 Gets 30 FPS on an RTX 5080 With Frame Gen Disabled
articles.summary: The Witcher 3 Remastered comes out tomorrow with a whole host of improvements that yet again bring it into the current generation. But it seems like if you want to max the game out with path tracing, you're going to need an absolute beast of a gaming PC.
articles.body:
The Witcher 3 Remastered comes out tomorrow with a whole host of improvements that yet again bring it into the current generation. But it seems like if you want to max the game out with path tracing, you're going to need an absolute beast of a gaming PC.

CD Projekt Red updated The Witcher 3 system requirements ahead of tomorrow's update, and while it is still reasonable on the low end, if you want to enable path tracing at 4K, you're going to need an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 , which is going for about $1,650 on the low end right now. Even with that beefy graphics card, the system requirements suggest that you'll need both DLSS upscaling and frame generation to hit 60 fps, which means Nvidia's penultimate GPU still struggles with the 11-year-old game.

So, I of course plugged in an RTX 5080 to see how the game runs with path tracing in a lap around Novigrad, and it isn't great. At 4K with everything enabled, including path tracing and hairworks, with DLSS upscaling set to 'Performance,' the Nvidia 5080 gets an average of 30 fps. That goes up to 59 fps with frame generation, but at that low of a base frame rate, there are some very noticeable artifacts, particularly in the ground textures.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered Screenshots

To be fair, hairworks has been nuking frame rates in The Witcher 3 since it first launched back in the day. You can (and probably should) disable hairworks to get much better performance, but even then, the 5080 can't hit 60 fps without frame gen. With hairworks disabled and path tracing enabled at 4K with DLSS set to performance, the game manages a 44 fps average, which jumps to 80 fps when frame generation is enabled.

The best way to get good performance out of The Witcher 3 Remastered right now, short of buying an RTX 5090 , is to disable path tracing entirely. When you do that on the RTX 5080, the frame rate jumps to 55 fps, which is more reasonable, especially considering that all of this testing was done in Novigrad, which has been notorious for performance issues since 2015. Keep in mind that even with path tracing disabled, there are a ton of other ray tracing effects that you can disable to further improve your performance.

Luckily, the new system requirements suggest that the game will scale down well to lower hardware. It'll just be a question of which settings you are willing to disable to get good performance from this massive game. Still, it does sting to play an 11-year-old game with one of the most expensive graphics cards on the market and not be able to max everything out at a good frame rate.

We've got plenty more on The Witcher 3 Remastered, including a roundup of all the improvements , and the global release times . The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered is available as a free update on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2 from September 29. To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the things The Witcher 3 doesn’t tell you , plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 walkthrough and The Witcher 3 endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 sex and romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher gear locations , Places of Power locations , and even Gwent card locations .

articles.title: The Last of Us Day Reveals Ghost of Yotei Collab Content and Ambience Video as Fans Beg Naughty Dog for TLOU 3
articles.summary: Naughty Dog has revealed it's celebrating The Last of Us Day 2026 with Ghost of Yotei content, player avatars on PlayStation and Steam, and an hour-long ambience video as fans continue begging for any updates on The Last of Us Part 3.
articles.body:
Naughty Dog has revealed that it's celebrating The Last of Us Day 2026 with Ghost of Yotei content, player avatars on PlayStation and Steam, and an hour-long ambience video as fans continue begging for any updates on The Last of Us Part 3.

It's… probably not what you or anyone else was expecting to see when the Sony studio teased plans for its annual holiday over the weekend . Instead of confirmation for The Last of Us Part 3 (or even yet, another remaster of an existing title), Naughty Dog instead revealed a collection of smaller surprises to keep fans tied over.

The headline is no doubt an armor set that's coming to Sucker Punch Productions' Ghost of Yotei. Available starting October 1, players will be able to hop into the sequel's Most Wanted mode while sporting Clicker-inspired armor. After it's unlocked, players will be able to use it in the base game, as well as its new Echoes of Sekigahara DLC. You can see a first look at The Last of Us armor below.

So, what else is there for The Last of Us Day 2026? Naughty Dog also announced a partnership with collectible company Youtooz for a Bloody Clicker figure. In addition to the previously revealed Welcome Hub background wallpaper for PS5, PlayStation users can enjoy four new themed avatars, with even more available on PC via Steam.

Also starting October 1 at 10 AM PDT / 1 PM EDT is a new Steam and Epic Games Store sale, which will discount The Last of Us Part 1 by 50% and The Last of Us Part 2 by 33%. There's also a new hour-long subway ambiance video for those who miss living in the series' Cordyceps-infested world. Does any of this come with a tease for The Last of Us Part 3? Well, no. Not at all.

It's been more than six years since Naughty Dog released The Last of Us Part 2, the series' latest entry. While the time between has seen the launch of important installments in the groundbreaking post-apocalyptic franchise, including the launch of two seasons for its live-action HBO adaptation , it's also brought disappointment for fans.

Perhaps the biggest blow to those hoping to hear more about where the franchise is heading was the cancellation of the long-in-development multiplayer spinoff , which many referred to as The Last of Us Online . Sony officially pulled the plug in December 2023, with Naughty Dog team promising it would focus solely on single-player games going forward.

As The Last of Us Part 3 remains absent and without any official confirmation that it's even in development, the studio is still very much in the weeds of its next new IP, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet . Initial footage for the project seemed promising when it was shown off in 2024 , but two years later, we still know little about it, too.

In addition to all of today's aforementioned goodies and a No Return charity stream for AbleGamers, the studio also announced it has established dedicated The Last of Us social media pages across Instagram , Facebook , and X/Twitter . Still, fans spent the days leading up to The Last of Us Day hoping the holiday would come with any news about the future of the series. Some hoped it might come with confirmation that The Last of Us Part 3 was in the works at all, but for now, at least, it seems fans will have to wait.

The future of The Last of Us continues to be a mystery as Naughty Dog celebrates The Last of Us Day 2026. In the meantime, you can see why some fans think a tease from Neil Druckmann suggests a third game will happen eventually . You can also read up on the multiplayer mod canceled at Sony's request earlier this month, and the new cast members that joined the show's third season .

articles.title: The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset With Infinite Battery Life Drops Below $200
articles.summary: My favorite gaming headset at its lowest price ever.
articles.body:
One of the best wireless gaming headsets just dropped to its lowest price ever. Woot, which is owned by Amazon, is offering a new Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro wireless gaming headset for PS5, PS4, and PC for just $191.99 after you apply 20% off coupon code " CHEERS ". If you're a first time Woot customer, the discount increases to 30%. Amazon Prime members get free shipping, otherwise add $5 for delivery. This is a new headset that comes with a 90-day Woot warranty.

SteelSeries Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset for $192 (or Less)

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset (PS5, PC)

The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro has long been one of IGN's highest rated wireless gaming headsets . IGN's Kevin Lee gave the Nova Pro a 10/10 "Masterpiece" review and I believe it still holds today. I've clocked well over a thousand hours on mine to the point that my earcups were worn through (I replaced them with the awesome WC Freeze gel earpads ). SteelSeries released a successor - the Nova Pro Omni - earlier this year, but it currently sells for $380 and the improvements are certainly not worth the nearly $200 price premium. The Omni's pièce de résistance is its seamless cross-platform switching. If you predominantly use these headphones for one platform, then stick with the Nova Pros.

The one feature that undoubtedly makes the Nova Pro stand out amongst the crowd is the ingenious hot-swappable battery system . The Nova Pro includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your headset and the other to remain charged and ready to go in a base station that doubles as a charger. This way, you get wireless freedom with zero downtime . Each battery lasts for up to 22 hours of continued use so you don't need to swap out too often.

The base station deserves additional mention. Not only does it charge your battery, it also features a clear and legible OLED display and a handy volume control knob. On the rear are USB inputs for connecting to your PC as well as an optional 3.5mm passthrough should you want to connect your speakers directly to the base station.

Of course a high end gaming headset is no good if it can't produce great sound and deliver vocal clarity. The Nova Pro is first and foremost a gaming headset, and it delivers big sound with its big 40mm neodymium dynamic drivers and 360° spatial sound effects (via SteelSeries Sonar for PC, Tempest 3D Audio for PS5, and Microsoft Spatial Sound for Xbox). The retractable boom mic is clear without any static and does a great job of canceling out ambient noise. My friends regularly point out that I sound like I'm in a quiet room because they hear nothing but my voice.

The Nova Pro is comfortable to use even during gaming marathons thanks to the suspension-style headband and comfortable leatherette ear cushions. You don't have to worry about babying it either, since the headband has a steel inner core. I've tossed mine around more times than I should have and it's still functionally perfect.

articles.body:
Editor's Note: This article is sponsored by CORSAIR.

For one week only, CORSAIR is offering discounts of up to $1,000 off select VENGEANCE and CORSAIR ONE prebuilt gaming PCs featuring NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 series graphics cards. These systems are professionally assembled by hand and feature brand-name components, including CORSAIR's very own cases, cooling systems, fans, and power supplies. The parts are non-proprietary so the system can be upgraded down the line, a major advantage compared to gaming consoles or other bespoke PC brands. All systems are backed by a 2-year warranty and lifetime technical support.

Save Up to $1,000 Off CORSAIR Gaming PCs

VENGEANCE a7500 AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D RTX 5080 Gaming PC (32GB/2TB)

VENGEANCE a7500 AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D RTX 5070 Gaming PC (32GB/1TB)

VENGEANCE i7600 Intel Core Ultra 7 265KF RTX 5080 Gaming PC (32GB/2TB)

CORSAIR ONE a600 PC AMD Ryzen 9 9900X3D RTX 5080 Gaming PC (32GB/2TB)

This particular VENGEANCE a7500 configuration has the biggest discount at $1,000 off. It's equipped with an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D CPU, GeForce RTX 5080 16GB GPU, 32GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 2TB SSD. Highlights include a NAUTILUS 240mm liquid CPU cooler, six RGB fans, and a 1000W 80 Plus Gold power supply, all housed in a CORSAIR 3500X midtower case.

The VENGEANCE i7600 is similar to the a7500 above (and it's $900 off), but with an Intel Core Ultra 7 256KF processor instead of an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D. Both Intel and AMD CPUs are overall excellent processors that complement the 5080 well. The Intel Core Ultra 7 256KF is more versatile for non-gaming applications since it has considerably more cores (20 cores vs 8 cores), but the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D performs better at gaming specifically thanks to its 3D V-cache.

The GeForce RTX 5080 GPU will run any game in 4K

Performance-wise, the RTX 5080 is no slouch. It's one of the fastest cards on the market, bested only by the $2,000 RTX 5090 and the discontinued $1,600 RTX 4090. You'll be able to play latest, most demanding games in 4K resolution at high settings and ray tracing enabled. The DLSS 4.5 update has further optimized multi-frame gen and upscaling so you can push really high framerates even in 4K. Check out our RTX 5080 review for our hands-on impressions.

The second VENGEANCE a7500 configuration is $400 off. This is a more affordable model equipped with a GeForce RTX 5070 12GB GPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, and 850W 80 Plus Gold power supply. The CPU remains the same, which is a very good thing because the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D is one of the best gaming CPUs you can buy at the moment.

The GeForce RTX 5070 GPU is an excellent choice for 1080p or 1440p gaming

The GeForce RTX 5070 is an outstanding graphics card for 1080p and 1440p gaming. It's also powerful enough to run most games at 4K, although at that point you'll see noticeable gains jumping up to a 5070 Ti. Compared to the previous generation GPUs, the RTX 5070 offers a slight performance improvement over the RTX 4070 Super, which was and still is an excellent GPU. Check out our RTX 5070 review .

The CORSAIR ONE eschews the two prevailing gaming PC ideologies that "bigger is better" and "RGB is life". It's housed in a custom compact case with minimal lighting effects and, instead, an elegant monolithic aluminum exerior that fits and looks great on any sized gaming desk. This configuration is equipped with a liquid-cooled AMD Ryzen 9 9900X3D CPU, GeForce RTX 5080 16GB GPU, 32GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 2TB SSD. A 1,000W SFX 80 Plus Gold PSU powers the system.

articles.title: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past EP Drops, Giving First Taste of New Music from the Expansion
articles.summary: Milan Records has released a five-track EP of new original music from The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion. Titled The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Songs of the Past (Original Soundtrack Gamescom 2026 EP), the first taste of the DLC's soundtrack includes compositions from Magda Urbanska, Marcin Pryzbylowicz, and Daniel Elms.
articles.body:
Milan Records has released a five-track EP of new original music from The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion. Titled The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Songs of the Past (Original Soundtrack Gamescom 2026 EP), the first taste of the DLC's soundtrack includes compositions from Magda Urbanska, Marcin Pryzbylowicz, and Daniel Elms.

"I’ve worked with classical music for most of my life," Urbanska said. "But folk requires a completely different sensibility — it has its own tone and form, while also offering enormous creative freedom. But our roots, our Slavic heritage, are something more than that — something that runs deep within us, something that grows out of who we are. I hope we’ve managed to preserve The Witcher DNA in these pieces."

Publisher Milan Records describes the new music as such: "Created to accompany Geralt of Rivia's return to the Path, the soundtrack expands upon the rich musical identity that has made The Witcher franchise a global phenomenon. Blending evocative orchestral writing with traditional folk influences, powerful vocal performances, and regional instrumentation inspired by the world's diverse cultures, the score captures both the intimacy and grandeur of a new chapter in Geralt's story." Here's the tracklist of the EP, which you can hear now everywhere :

Songs of the Past was a nearly unprecedented announcement earlier this year (though it had been rumored ): a new expansion for a game that will be 12 years old by the time Songs of the Past ships next year, and the first expansion in over a decade. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was named IGN's Game of the Year in 2015 .

articles.title: Corsair's Vanguard Air 99 Gaming Keyboard Is Already £50 Off at Amazon UK Ahead of Prime Big Deal Days
articles.summary: Score an early Amazon Prime Big Deal Days discount on the premium Corsair Vanguard Air 99 wireless gaming keyboard. Save £50 on this low-profile mechanical keyboard in the UK before the main event begins.
articles.body:
Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days doesn't officially begin until October 6, but we're already seeing some early discounts ahead of the two-day event, including a sizeable saving on one of Corsair's latest gaming keyboards.

The Corsair Vanguard Air 99 is currently £189.99 at Amazon UK , down from £239.99. That's a £50 saving before the main Prime Big Deal Days sale has even got underway, making this one to keep an eye on if you've been considering a premium gaming keyboard.

Corsair VANGUARD AIR 99 WIRELESS RGB Gaming Keyboard

Corsair's Vanguard Air 99 Keyboard Is Already £50 Off

Corsair isn't exactly known for making budget gaming peripherals, and the Vanguard Air 99 is very much aimed at the higher end of the keyboard market. It's a premium wireless gaming keyboard built for players who want a combination of performance, customisation and a few more bells and whistles than you'll find on a basic mechanical board.

The keyboard uses Corsair's MLX Pulse linear mechanical switches, with the low-profile design aimed at delivering fast and responsive inputs while keeping things relatively quiet. There's also a 8,000Hz polling rate, which means the keyboard can report inputs extremely quickly, helping minimise latency when you're gaming.

It's a 96% layout, too, giving you a more compact footprint than a traditional full-sized keyboard while retaining the dedicated arrow keys and number pad. That makes it a potentially good middle ground if you don't want to sacrifice functionality just to save a bit of desk space.

The Vanguard Air 99 is also wireless, with both 2.4GHz wireless and Bluetooth connectivity available, so you can use it across different devices without having to keep a cable permanently attached to your desk.

As you'd expect from a modern Corsair keyboard, there's per-key RGB lighting and plenty of scope for customisation through Corsair's software. You can also expect the sort of build quality you'd hope for at this price, with the Vanguard Air 99 designed as a premium option rather than an entry-level gaming keyboard.

articles.title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Is 'Testing the Bounds' of What Naughty Dog Is Capable of, Troy Baker Says
articles.summary: Troy Baker has teased that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is "testing the bounds" of what Naughty Dog is capable of, telling fans that they are going to have their "minds blown."
articles.body:
Troy Baker has teased that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is "testing the bounds" of what Naughty Dog is capable of, telling fans that they are going to have their "minds blown."

The Last of Us actor, who is also featured in the studio's new sci-fi adventure , talked about what the studio is cooking up during an appearance at Ottawa Comiccon in Ontario, Canada, earlier this month. Footage of his panel was captured and shared on YouTube before clips made their way around social media today, but the biggest highlight from the hour-long talk saw Baker teasing Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet.

"You guys are going to have your minds blown," he said. Covering his mouth and closing his eyes, he added, "You are not ready. You are not ready. It's so good."

Baker noted that, as previously announced, Naughty Dog recently wrapped shooting performance capture for the studio's new IP . Of all of the things to call attention to, though, it's star Tati Gabrielle and her work as main character, Jordan A. Mun.

"I don't know how [writer and director Neil Druckmann] found two amazing actors," he added, referencing Ashley's Johnson's casting as Ellie in The Last of Us. "He found Ashley for Ellie, and he found Tati for Jordan. It's like, what? How do you do that?

"She is the spiritual successor. There is so much about Jordan and that game of Intergalactic that feels like… man, I feel all of it. I feel Uncharted, I feel The Last of Us, I feel something new. They are testing the bounds of what that studio is capable of. Everything that I've seen, they are delivering, and it's going to be incredible."

We know precious little about Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet since Naughty Dog first revealed it at The Game Awards 2024. Druckmann called the new game " incredible " in 2025, and later that same year, he joked that he's been "bootcamp-ing" Gabrielle on the hate the studio's received regarding The Last of Us Part 2 . He also said he was stepping away from HBO's The Last of Us show to pour his focus into the project's development .

Despite calling it the "most ambitious game" the team has made to date , the only actual look at it we've seen arrived in that first reveal trailer. Despite there being no firm release date, as Naughty Dog no-shows State of Plays and goes on seven years without a new game release , there are at least a few reasons to suspect we'll learn more in the somewhat near future.

We knew Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet would miss 2026, but there have been rumors that the PlayStation developer is shooting for a 2027 launch. Wrapping up work on performance capture just last month means that progress is moving steadily ahead, too. The Last of Us Part 2 reached a similar milestone one year before its 2020 launch in 2019, so if the team is following that same trajectory, there is at least hope we'll learn more in the months ahead.

Unfortunately, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet has no official launch schedule in place for now. In the meantime, The Last of Us Day 2026 has given fans a little something to chew on while they await the series' return. The series' future is something Baker touched on during his convention appearance, too.

"We'll see," he said, crossing his fingers.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).
